sources.note: Covers Lalo varieties [ywt/yik/ywl] only; a full-text search for stress/accent finds no 'Xiangtang', 'Zhenkang' or 'Southern Lolopo'; 'stress' occurs only incidentally (a syllabic-nasal remark and a laryngoscopy citation). Not a source for ysp.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives OAI harvest (local cache and Hammarström's hh.bib (local cache _glottolog_bib/hh.bib), searched for 'ysp', 'Southern Lolopo', 'Xiangtang', 'Zhenkang'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No SIL item is tagged ysp (only a Lolopo [ycl] Webonary dictionary and Yang's Lalo works); hh.bib tags ysp only in Yang 2011, Bradley 2004, Xiao 1992 and Hammarström's Ethnologue-review appendix entry.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (English), 'Lolopo language', raw wikitext as of 2026-09-17 (Chinese Wikipedia '倮倮泼土语' also read online).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Its phonology tables are Yao'an Central Yi (Merrifield 2012, SIL) = Lolopo [ycl], not ysp. On ysp it only repeats Yang 2011 ms: 'Xiangtang 香堂 (spoken in Zhenkang County).. Jinggu, Zhenyuan, Pu'er, Jiangcheng, Mengla, Jinghong, and Zhenkang counties, with perhaps under 80,000 speakers' and 'Western Lolo (Southern Lolopo in Ethnologue)'.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Lolopo, Southern' [ysp]. Dallas: SIL International (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Gives population 190,000 (2002); location Yunnan: Jingdong, Jinggu, Lancang, Pu'er, Simao, Zhenyuan counties; classification Ngwi, Central; no bibliography.
